front: What does SFT change in a base model?
back: Behaviour (answer instructions in a given format), not knowledge. It trains on (prompt, response) demonstrations with a low learning rate for 1-3 epochs.
Loss only on response and end tokens; prompt labels set to an ignore index (-100). Avoids training the model to write instructions; prompt tokens remain in the context.
$\mathcal L=-\frac{1}{\sum M_t}\sum_t M_t\ln p(y_t\mid s_{\le t})$; divide by the number of supervised targets, not $B\cdot T$.

front: Inputs and labels for an SFT sequence
back: ids = prompt + response + [eos]; x = ids[:-1]; y = labels[1:] with prompt positions = -100. Padding targets are also -100.
Fine-tuning erases general ability. Use low LR, few epochs, mix in some pretraining data, or restrict updates (LoRA).
$W' = W + \frac{\alpha}{r}BA$ with $B:(d_{out},r)$, $A:(r,d_{in})$, $W$ frozen. Rank of the update $\le r$.
$r(d_{out}+d_{in})$ per adapted matrix instead of $d_{out}d_{in}$. Example 4096x4096, r=16: 131,072 = 0.78%.
$B=0$ (adapter starts at zero, model unchanged), $A$ random (so $\bar B\ne0$ and learning starts).
$\bar B=sG^\top h$, $\bar A=s(GB)^\top x$, $\bar x=GW+s(GB)A$, with $h=xA^\top$.
Keeps the magnitude of the update comparable across ranks, so runs of different rank can be compared without retuning the learning rate.
$W_{merged}=W+\frac{\alpha}{r}BA$: identical outputs, no extra latency. Or keep adapters separate to swap per task.
Frozen base weights stored in 4-bit (NF4, with double quantisation of the constants), LoRA adapters trained in higher precision, paged optimiser state.
A rank-r update cannot represent changes that need higher rank; tasks needing a lot of new knowledge may need larger r or full fine-tuning.

front: Why does full fine-tuning cost so much memory?
back: Gradients and optimiser state (Adam keeps two moments) for every weight: about 16 bytes/parameter in fp32 before activations.
